author: Robert Carr
description: Lemon-zaatar salmon with browned broccoli, roasted tomatoes, chewy barley, dill-tahini yogurt and pistachios. The citrus, herbs and creamy sauce are intended to make salmon approachable without relying on a salty glaze.
equipment: Instant-read thermometer, such as Thermapen ONE
Four shallow meal-prep containers and four small sauce containers

groceryIngredients.note: Choose an unseasoned 10-12-minute variety; not regular or hulled barley.
2.25 g total; use a fine salt weighing about 6 g per teaspoon.
Need 3 tablespoons juice and 2 teaspoons finely grated zest.
Four 5-ounce portions, thawed, pin bones removed, without added brine; nutrition will depend on species.

10 g; choose at most 120 mg sodium per teaspoon.

ingredients: Barley: 150 g dry quick-cooking barley, an unseasoned 10-12-minute variety
Barley finish: 1 tablespoon (15 mL) fresh lemon juice, 2 tablespoons (6 g) finely chopped fresh dill and 1/8 teaspoon (0.75 g) fine sea salt
Vegetables: 1 1/2 lb (680 g) broccoli florets, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces and dried
Vegetables: 12 oz (340 g) cherry tomatoes, left whole and dried
Vegetables: 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil, allocated as 2 teaspoons for broccoli and 1 teaspoon for tomatoes
Vegetables: 1/8 teaspoon (0.75 g) fine sea salt and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, both for the broccoli
Salmon: four 5-oz portions skinless salmon, 20 oz (567 g) total, thawed and pin bones removed
Salmon: 2 teaspoons extra-virgin olive oil and 2 teaspoons (10 g) Dijon mustard
Salmon: 1 1/2 tablespoons salt-free zaatar seasoning, 2 teaspoons finely grated lemon zest, 1/8 teaspoon (0.75 g) fine sea salt and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
Sauce: 170 g plain 2% Greek yogurt, about 3/4 cup
Sauce: 2 tablespoons (30 g) unsalted tahini, well stirred
Sauce: 2 tablespoons (30 g) fresh lemon juice
Sauce: 1 tablespoon plus 1 teaspoon (20 g) water
Sauce: 1 small garlic clove (4 g peeled), finely grated
Sauce: 2 tablespoons (6 g) finely chopped fresh dill
Finish: 3 tablespoons (24 g) chopped unsalted roasted pistachios
instructions: Start the oven and barley: Heat the oven to 425 F with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Bring 3 cups water to a boil in a medium saucepan. Add 150 g dry quick-cooking barley and simmer for the package's 10-12-minute cooking time, until tender with a little chew. Drain thoroughly. The timing assumes this quick-cooking variety, not regular barley.

Roast the vegetables: Toss 1 1/2 lb (680 g) dried broccoli florets with 2 teaspoons olive oil, 1/8 teaspoon (0.75 g) fine sea salt and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper on the first sheet pan. On the second pan, toss 12 oz (340 g) cherry tomatoes with 1 teaspoon olive oil. Spread each vegetable into a single layer. Put both pans in the preheated oven. Roast the broccoli for 22-28 minutes, turning it at 15 minutes; the tomatoes get a 10-minute head start before the salmon joins their pan.

Make the cold sauce while the vegetables roast: Whisk 170 g plain 2% Greek yogurt, 2 tablespoons (30 g) tahini, 2 tablespoons (30 g) lemon juice, 1 tablespoon plus 1 teaspoon (20 g) water, 4 g finely grated garlic and 2 tablespoons (6 g) chopped dill in a bowl. Scrape the sides thoroughly. These measured ingredients make about 260 g sauce. Refrigerate it while the hot food cooks.

Season the salmon: Pat four 5-oz salmon portions, 20 oz (567 g) total, thoroughly dry. Mix 2 teaspoons olive oil, 2 teaspoons (10 g) Dijon mustard, 1 1/2 tablespoons salt-free zaatar, 2 teaspoons lemon zest, 1/8 teaspoon (0.75 g) fine sea salt and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper directly over the tops and sides of the four portions, rubbing into a thin, even coating. Wash your hands and sanitize the raw-fish preparation area before handling cooked food or sauce.

Cook the salmon: After the tomatoes have roasted for 10 minutes, carefully move the tomatoes toward the pan's edges and place the four seasoned 5-oz salmon portions in the center without overlap. Roast for about 10-15 minutes, checking the thickest part of each portion at 10 minutes. Remove each portion when its center reaches 145 F. Do not keep cooking a finished portion while waiting for a thicker one. The tomatoes should be blistered and tender; the broccoli should have browned edges.
Finish the barley: Toss the cooked barley made from 150 g dry barley with 1 tablespoon (15 mL) lemon juice, 2 tablespoons (6 g) chopped dill and 1/8 teaspoon (0.75 g) fine sea salt.

Portion: Weigh the finished barley and distribute it evenly among four shallow containers; do the same with the cooked broccoli and tomatoes. Add one cooked salmon portion to each container. Pack about 65 g dill-tahini yogurt in each of four separate cups and 6 g chopped pistachios in each of four dry topping cups. Keep both toppings off the hot food until serving. Refrigerate the meal portions promptly as described in the notes.
notes: Timing: About 50 minutes total from starting preparation to portioning, including oven preheating. Use thawed salmon, ready-trimmed broccoli and 10-12-minute barley. Frozen-fish thawing is a separate advance step, not something completed inside the cooking time.

For a salmon newcomer: Buy fish with a fresh, mild smell. Strong sour, rancid, ammonia-like or distinctly off fishy odors are rejection signs, not something to cover with lemon or sauce. This recipe still tastes like salmon; a non-fishy result or a particular tasting score cannot be guaranteed.

Meal prep: Refrigerate shallow portions promptly at 40 F or colder, within 2 hours of cooking or 1 hour if the room is above 90 F. Do not leave food on the counter until completely cool. Keep the yogurt sauce refrigerated and the pistachios separate. Use refrigerated portions within 3-4 days.

Salmon quality: For the most cautious introduction to salmon, eat one portion freshly cooked. For later meals, properly chilled cooked salmon may be served cold with the yogurt sauce alongside the heated barley and vegetables. Repeated reheating is not necessary.

Freezing: Freeze any salmon/barley/vegetable portions not planned for the next 3-4 days on prep day. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator and use the next day. Keep the yogurt sauce refrigerated for its 3-4-day window rather than promising that it will freeze without separating.

Reheating: Remove the yogurt and pistachios. Add 1 tablespoon water to one hot-component portion, cover with a vented lid and microwave at medium power in short intervals. Check several places and reheat leftovers to 165 F; add the cold 65 g sauce and 6 g pistachios afterward. This safety endpoint can make reheated salmon firmer than freshly cooked salmon.

Portion options: For a smaller meal, reduce the dry barley from 150 g to 100 g for the batch and keep the fish and vegetables unchanged. For a larger meal, increase dry barley to 250 g and cooking water to 5 cups, still draining after the package cooking time. The nutrition estimate is for the base version, not these adjustments.

Health-conscious review: Salmon, barley, vegetables, measured olive oil, nuts and a low-fat yogurt sauce fit a heart-conscious eating pattern. Barley that is pearled or quick-cooking is not necessarily a whole grain. Overall sodium, saturated fat and calories across the day still matter; this meal does not promise a blood-pressure or weight change.

Food-safety basis: FDA Selecting and Serving Fresh and Frozen Seafood Safely, https://www.fda.gov/food/buy-store-serve-safe-food/selecting-and-serving-fresh-and-frozen-seafood-safely; USDA Leftovers and Food Safety, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/leftovers-and-food-safety.
Allergens: Fish, milk, sesame, pistachios, mustard and barley gluten. Original recipe developed for this collection; not kitchen-tested. Leave status as not-tried until cooked.

Flavor review: A thin measured Dijon coating helps the lemon-zaatar seasoning cling to the salmon. Zest supplies citrus aroma without an acidic overnight fish marinade. The 2 teaspoons mustard are included in the whole batch, not added to each serving. Mustard adds sodium, so the recipe does not increase its existing measured salt.

Salmon meal-prep quality: For your first trial, consider freezing the day-3 and day-4 fish portions promptly on prep day and thawing each overnight in the refrigerator before use. This is a flavor/texture preference, not an extension of the 3-4-day refrigerated safety window. Never try to improve an off-smelling fish portion with more seasoning.

Nutrition: Approximate per base serving, including the listed sauce, oil and toppings. Calculated using raw meat/fish weights, dry grain weights and about 500 g drained legumes per two cans, with USDA SR Legacy and representative product labels. Brands, cooking losses, drained yields and portion changes alter the result. The repository nutrition audit documents ingredient weights and explicit proxies; these estimates are not a medical certification or a kitchen test.

Water for reheating is a serving-time addition, separate from the cooking water in the ingredient list. Its measured 1 tablespoon per reheated portion adds no meaningful nutrients and is not a grocery purchase.
title: Zaatar-Pistachio Salmon with Lemon-Dill Barley
